question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Timed degron depletion to separate establishment from maintenance
ideas.description: Prime cells with a transient stimulus, then acutely degrade FOS/JUN (dTAG/AID) at different times after washout, before restimulation. If memory (faster or stronger transcription, retained accessibility) is lost upon late depletion, AP-1 is needed to maintain it, not only to set it up.

ideas.title: Pulse-pattern optogenetic AP-1 activation with memory readout
ideas.description: Use optogenetic or chemically gated AP-1 to deliver defined pulse numbers, durations and intervals, then test the response to a later challenge. Dependence on pulse history and a decay time constant would show AP-1 activity itself encodes memory, independent of upstream signaling.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-resolved tracking across divisions
ideas.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN together with a target-enhancer reporter, and follow sister cells through division after priming. Heritable differences in response, together with AP-1 mitotic retention, would test whether memory is carried by AP-1 or by downstream chromatin.

ideas.title: Motif-level CRISPR editing plus synthetic AP-1 recruitment
ideas.description: Delete or mutate AP-1 motifs at specific memory enhancers and ask if priming is lost. Conversely, recruit AP-1 to a neutral locus with dCas9 and ask if it creates a persistent, restimulation-competent state. This tests necessity and sufficiency at the locus level.

ideas.title: Hysteresis and bistability of the FOS/JUN feedback circuit
ideas.description: Measure single-cell dose-response with increasing versus decreasing stimulus, and perturb the FOS/JUN autoregulatory loop while fitting a mathematical model. Bimodality and hysteresis dependent on the loop would support a self-sustaining circuit memory that does not need a chromatin mark.

candidates: Time-course ChIP/CUT&RUN of AP-1 (FOS/JUN) occupancy after transient stimulus and after washout
ATAC-seq footprinting of AP-1 motifs at memory loci days after stimulus removal
Acute degron (dTAG/AID) depletion of FOS/JUN after stimulus to test maintenance vs. establishment of accessibility
Optogenetic pulsed AP-1 activation with varying pulse patterns to test history dependence
Single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) tracking of primed vs naive cells upon restimulation
Live-cell imaging of endogenously tagged FOS/JUN with reporter of target gene to measure memory across divisions
Mitotic bookmarking assay: imaging/ChIP of AP-1 on mitotic chromosomes
Dominant-negative (A-FOS) induced at different times to separate initiation from maintenance
CRISPR mutation of AP-1 motifs at individual enhancers followed by prime-restimulate assays
dCas9-based synthetic recruitment of AP-1 to a neutral locus to test sufficiency for creating memory
Histone mark profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) with and without AP-1 depletion during memory
Hi-C/Micro-C to see AP-1-dependent enhancer-promoter loops persisting after stimulus
Pioneer-like activity test: nucleosome positioning (MNase) at AP-1 sites after transient binding
Mathematical modeling of AP-1 positive feedback (FOS/JUN autoregulation) bistability and hysteresis
Dose-response hysteresis measurements in single cells to detect bistable switch
Proteomics of AP-1 partner switching (BAF, p300) over time after stimulus
Lineage tracing/clonal analysis of memory inheritance in sister cells
In vivo memory test: primed tissue (skin/macrophage) with AP-1 inhibitor given during memory period before rechallenge
Comparing AP-1 family member dynamics (FOSB, ΔFOSB stable isoform) as persistent molecular carriers
Cross-species/cell-type comparison of AP-1 motif architecture in memory-capable vs non-capable enhancers
